answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may place bids, with acceptance weighted by stake and a portion slashed when independently audited work is fraudulent. One operator can still create many accounts, but must fund each and risks losing capital for cheating, so splitting into sybils no longer multiplies influence for free. The stake sets a zenith on affordable identities; an attacker may wander across accounts, but cannot evade the shared cost any more than a river escapes its channel.
